text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- More reaction to new press law. Union heads say they will resign on May 24.
- Arab Bank to announce formally today establishment of Arab Islamic Bank International with paid up capital of 40 million dinars ($56 million).
- Crown Prince Hassan, visiting Rome, says Middle East peace process is going through a severe crisis.
- Unions, opposition parliamentarians and political parties show solidarity with journalists over press law.
- Jordan and Israel agree to expand Aqaba airport.
- Economic mission leaves today for negotiations on Paris Club debt rescheduling.
- Thousands of claims from returnees from 1990-1991 Gulf War. Another tranche of $95 million of compensation expected to arrive in July.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says announcement expected soon of U.S. aid to Jordan.
- Crown Prince Hassan discusses EU's role in peace process and bilateral relations. Jordan signs two agreements of cooperation with Italy.
- All 12 presidents of professional associations will resign if government does not reverse press and publications law.
